title: NorthStar Labs POC - Capacity & Autoscale Scoping
summary: POC scoping to size reserved GPU capacity, define burst strategy and fallback policies. Agreement on success criteria (latency SLOs, cost targets, throughput), benchmark plan, and a 3-week timeline for the pilot. Action items: Redwood to send pricing, benchmark harness and security docs; customer to provide sample load profile and CSV of request distribution.
topics: POC success criteria: latency, cost, throughput, error rates
Workload sizing: qps, token distributions, peak vs baseline
Reserved GPUs vs burst capacity: commit size, warm pools
Autoscaling policies: scale up/down thresholds, cool-downs
Fallback policies: model downgrades, regional failover
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-18
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Sara Kim (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jenna Park (NorthStar Eng Mgr), Ravi Patel (NorthStar ML Infra), Liam O'Neill (NorthStar SRE)

Summary (auto): Quick sync to scope POC capacity and autoscale behavior. Goal to validate latency SLOs under realistic traffic and prove cost per-1k tokens.

00:00 Sara Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm sara from redwood, i'll run through goals, marco will do the infra deep dive, um if we can go around quick intros?
00:12 Jenna Park: hi jenna here, eng manager for inference team at northstar, we're leading the POC.
00:18 Ravi Patel: ravi, ml infra, i'll own the benchmark runs and provide the load profile.
00:23 Marco Alvarez: marco, solutions engineer at redwood, i'll map the autoscale and capacity options.

01:05 Sara Kim: high level - this POC is to validate capacity sizing. we typically do a reserved baseline + burst pool, and we want to make sure that with your qps and token distro you hit the 95th perc latency targets without overspending, right?
01:19 Jenna Park: yep, correct. our main success criteria are: p95 generation latency < 350ms for short prompts (~256 tokens), < 1.2s for long ones (~1024 tokens), throughput of 40 reqs/sec sustained, and cost per 1k tokens under our internal threshold. also <1% error rate.
01:45 Marco Alvarez: ok good, that matches typical enterprise asks. couple clarifying q's - what's peak vs baseline qps and typical sequence length distribution?
01:53 Ravi Patel: baseline is 8-12 qps, peak bursts to ~60 qps during business hours for 10-15 min periods. token distro is bimodal: about 65% <=256 tokens, 25% 256-512, 10% 512-1200.
02:18 Marco Alvarez: perfect. so for sizing we look at sustained capacity and then a burst strategy. for reserved we recommend sizing to cover baseline + buffer, so you'd reserve GPUs to handle ~15 qps steady. then configure a burst pool (reserved pre-warmed instances or on-demand) to handle up to the 60 qps peaks.
02:40 Jenna Park: can you be more specific on GPU types? we run H100s on prem but cloud options vary.
02:47 Marco Alvarez: yes, for gen models we've seen H100 or A100 80GB perf. For your mix i'd recommend dedicating 2x A100-80 or 1x H100 per reserved pool node depending on model and quantization. rough rule of thumb: one A100-80 with our optimized runtime handles ~12-18 small requests/sec for 512-token avg workloads with batching enabled.
03:14 Liam O'Neill: how does batching affect latency? we can't sacrifice p95; sometimes batching adds wait time.
03:21 Marco Alvarez: right, we use adaptive batching with latency caps. for p95 targets we'll set max batch delay at 15ms and batch size cap so tail latency stays under your SLO. also prefix/KV caching will help with repeated prompts. note: in some transcriptions KV cache got written as KV cash - sorry, autocap.
03:45 Sara Kim: also fallback policies: if burst capacity exhausted we can route to smaller model variant (quantized) or to hosted fallback region, or queue with a best-effort flag. which is preferred?
03:58 Jenna Park: prefer smaller model fallback over queuing for user-facing flows, but for lower priority background tasks queuing is fine.
04:10 Marco Alvarez: good. so for the POC we'll test three modes: (1) reserved-only, (2) reserved + burst with warm pool, (3) reserved + burst + model-downgrade fallback. we'll measure p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies and error rates.

06:05 Ravi Patel: question on warm pools - how long do nodes need to be warm to avoid cold-start issues?
06:12 Marco Alvarez: with our runtime, warm pool nodes should keep a warm kv cache and model loaded — ~5-10 minutes of idle is fine. cold start for large model can be 30-90s if you pull weights from scratch, so we recommend keeping a small warm pool for burst windows.
06:30 Jenna Park: cost implications? pre-warmed vs on-demand is expensive.
06:34 Sara Kim: yes, that's why recommended approach is reserved baseline to minimize cost + small warm pool sized by expected burst frequency. we can provide a cost model with expected token consumption and node hours — we'll send an example spreadsheet.
06:47 Marco Alvarez: action: benchmark plan — two runs: synthetic load that matches your token distro, and a replay from production traces (you to send). we'll collect tail latencies and throughput.
07:05 Jenna Park: timeline?
07:09 Sara Kim: we propose a 3-week POC: week 0 prep and baseline data share, week 1 reserved + basic run, week 2 burst tests and fallbacks, plus one day for joint analysis and final report. can compress to 2 weeks if you provide traces ASAP.
07:28 Ravi Patel: we can share traces by monday.
07:32 Sara Kim: perfect. next on security: SSO, audit logs, KMS? any red flags?
07:40 Liam O'Neill: we need KMS integration, SOC2 + ISO27001 docs, and VPC peering for private deployments. for this POC we prefer dedicated private connection but open to hosted with strict retention.
07:54 Marco Alvarez: we support customer-managed KMS, VPC peering, and have SOC2 compliance pack — will send security whitepaper and certs. note some product names sometimes get misspelled in transcripts — e.g., Redwood Dedicated becomes Redwood Dedicate in notes.
08:10 Jenna Park: what about monitoring? we need per-token cost, per-route latency, and tracing.
08:18 Marco Alvarez: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model dashboards, per-route SLOs, and tracing hooks. we'll give you a demo link and a sandbox account for the POC.

10:00 Sara Kim: quick recap of success criteria so we align:
- p95 gen latency < 350ms short, < 1.2s long
- sustain 40 req/sec with peaks to 60 qps
- cost per 1k tokens within your threshold (we'll model)
- error rate <1%

10:30 Jenna Park: agreed.

11:00 Marco Alvarez: benchmarks: we'll produce CSVs of latency distributions, token counts, and cost estimates. we recommend measuring cold-start percent of requests as a metric too.

12:10 Ravi Patel: any recommended autoscale policy parameters?
12:18 Marco Alvarez: sample: scale-up when 2-minute avg queue time > 50ms OR CPU/GPU util > 65% for 30s, scale-down when util < 25% for 5 minutes, cool-down 3 minutes. for burst windows use fast-add (spin up N nodes) with pre-warm flag. these are starting points — we'll tune during POC.

15:05 Sara Kim: fallback specifics: model downgrade to a quantized 4-bit variant for non-critical features; region fallback to secondary region (eu-west to us-east) if capacity exhausted; and request tagging to separate high/low priority.
15:30 Jenna Park: good to know. how deep is instrumentation? we need per-token trace to match cost accounting.
15:36 Marco Alvarez: we can instrument token-level costs and associate them with request ids. we'll share sample dashboard screenshots.

18:00 Liam O'Neill: what about SLA for Dedicated vs Hosted for POC?
18:06 Sara Kim: POC uses dev-level SLA; Dedicated reserved pools could be backed by SLA for production later. For POC we'll provide monitoring and support during benchmark windows.

20:00 Sara Kim: alright last section - next steps and action items.
20:10 Marco Alvarez: ok i'll be the SE contact for benchmarks. i'll prepare the benchmark harness and a sample config for autoscale policies and warm pool sizing.
20:22 Sara Kim: i'll send pricing and cost model spreadsheet, and security pack (SOC2, KMS integration guide), and a sandbox console invite.
20:30 Jenna Park: we'll share traces and a CSV of qps/time-of-day distribution by monday.
20:36 Ravi Patel: we'll also confirm which model variants we want to test (base, quantized 4-bit, and a smaller distil variant).

End of transcript.
